# Customer Problem Interview — Non-leading Guide

**Use only after owner authorizes outreach.** No automated contacting, scraping emails or collecting sensitive data. Obtain informed consent for notes; avoid recording names or confidential details unless necessary and agreed.

## Recruitment record

Target role, industry, organization size, current alternative, why recruited, consent and date. Avoid seeking friends who will just encourage the idea.

## Interview structure (20–30 minutes)

1. 'Walk me through the last time you needed to **[specific job]**.'
2. 'What triggered it? What tools, people and files were involved?'
3. 'What took the most time or caused an error? How often does it happen?'
4. 'What happens if you don't solve it?'
5. 'What did you try to make it easier? Why did it work or fail?'
6. 'What do you use today and what does it cost in money and effort?'
7. 'Who chooses or approves new tools? What would make switching hard?'
8. 'Can you show a **sanitized** example or demonstrate the workflow without exposing private data?'
9. 'What would you do if there were no new tool available?'
10. 'Would you agree to a follow-up task test or pilot if it proved useful?' (Do not frame interest as purchase.)

## Avoid

'Would you use my app?', 'Would you pay $X for an AI solution?', hypothetical feature wishlists, pressure to compliment the developer. Ask about **past behavior**, not imagined intentions.

## After each interview

Summarize facts, exact anonymized quotes (only with consent), contradictions, current costs, urgency, buying authority, willingness to trial, and unresolved questions. Distinguish *stated intention* from actual commitment. Do not store private student/customer/media data.
